slides.title: Reading state from continuous behavior
slides.notes: Title. Say in one sentence why you picked this paper, tied to this lab's work.

slides.headline: Why the question has not been answerable
lines: The measurement everyone uses is taken twice: at the start and at the end.
Everything the individual did in between is discarded.
This paper records all of it — and predicts the endpoint from the middle.
slides.notes:
CLAIM — the gap.
MY READ — this is the promise; say the punchline now so the methods that follow read as evidence rather than as a toll.
IF SHORT — never cut.

slides.headline: One subject, recorded continuously, one day at a time
slides.takeaway: Continuous recording turns a two-point comparison into a dense time series per individual.
slides.notes:
CLAIM — what was recorded.
POINT — the trough, then the plateau.
SAY — 24 h, 1 Hz, n = 40.
IF SHORT — 45 s.

slides.headline: How many components does the representation need
slides.takeaway: Variance explained saturates by about eight components, so eight is what the rest of the analysis uses.
slides.notes:
CLAIM — model order chosen by saturation, not by task performance.
SAY — >90% by 8 components.
MY READ — an elbow is a weak criterion; say so.
IF SHORT — cut, it is on backup.

slides.headline: The first half of every life looks alike
slides.takeaway: State usage is stable early; the interesting structure is in the half you cannot see yet.
slides.notes: Build step 1 of 2 — reveal the early half, ask what they expect next, then advance.

slides.headline: The first half of every life looks alike
slides.takeaway: State usage is stable early; the interesting structure is in the half you cannot see yet.
slides.notes: Build step 2 of 2 — the full record. PAUSE — take two predictions before moving on.

slides.headline: The two groups separate long before the endpoint
slides.takeaway: Trajectories diverge early, and the group difference is already measurable at a fixed early age.
slides.notes:
CLAIM — early separation.
POINT — where the two colours part, then the two means.
SAY — P < 0.0001 at fixed age.
PAUSE — ask what would convince them this is not circular.

slides.headline: A model estimates the endpoint from the middle at R = 0.94
slides.takeaway: Held-out estimates track the truth closely — but the model was trained on the endpoint, so that is what it measures.
slides.notes:
CLAIM — the payoff.
SAY — R = 0.94, leave-one-subject-out.
MY READ — accuracy is not mechanism.
DELIVER — fast, do not pause here.

slides.headline: The middle of the record carries the endpoint
bullets: Continuous recording, one subject at a time, for the whole interval.
Eight components summarize a day; a life becomes a trajectory.
Groups separate early, before any endpoint is observable.
A held-out model estimates the endpoint at R = 0.94.
slides.notes: Summary. The headline is the assertion the talk earned — not the word 'Summary'.

slides.headline: For discussion: what this design can and cannot support
lines: The group label is retrospective; nothing here is an intervention.
One cohort, one site — the model order may not transfer.
For us: is the win the timescale, or the representation?
slides.notes: Parking lot. Say 'hold that — it's on my last slide' during the talk.

slides.takeaway: Variance explained versus model order, with the elbow marked.
